content.intro: This lesson covers Interrupts and Shared Hardware State. It sits in Module 25, Embedded Rust and no_std, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Interrupts and Shared Hardware State matters when you work with target-specific resource and hardware constraints. content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Embedded Rust must fit the target’s processor, memory, timing, and hardware constraints. no_std removes the standard library, so available APIs and startup/linking responsibilities depend on the target.
